div.div:
No AWS access key. No IAM role.
No boto3 credential chain. No SigV4.
The app speaks one API to one endpoint,
whatever the model behind it turns out to be.

div.div:
• Authenticate the gateway key
• Resolve default-bedrock
• Check the model is on the allowlist
• Check budget and rate limits
• Apply guardrails
• Translate the request to the Bedrock
API shape and sign it with the
integration's IAM credential
• Meter tokens, cost, and latency
• Write the prompt and response log

div.div:
Basic information
Name, Description
Slug default-bedrock — what the app names in the call
Credential stays here, never handed out
AWS access key ID · AWS secret access key · Region
Model provisioning
All models, or an explicit allowlist. Everything not on
the list is unreachable through this integration.
Workspace provisioning
Which teams see Bedrock in their Model Catalog, and
each team's budget and rate limit.
Pricing adjust multiplier
Your negotiated AWS rate, or an internal showback markup.

div.div:
1. AWS bills you for Bedrock inference. Unchanged by the gateway.
Same account, same rates, same Cost Explorer line item.
2. Palo Alto Networks meters flex credits by token volume.
1 token = 4 characters. Prompts, MCP, and agent-to-agent traffic
all count. Identical pricing for SaaS and Hybrid.
The dollar figures in the AI Gateway dashboard are the provider cost
it calculates for you, optionally adjusted by your multiplier. They are
not your flex credit consumption. Those are two different numbers
in two different places.

div.div:
SaaS app → PANW-hosted gateway → Bedrock in your region.
The prompt leaves your environment before it reaches AWS, even
though Bedrock itself is inside your own account. For a customer who
chose Bedrock specifically to keep inference in their account, this is
the conversation to have early, not at cutover.
Hybrid app → gateway pod in your cluster → Bedrock. The prompt
never leaves your environment, and prompt logs can be written to a
bucket you own. Only control-plane configuration and metering reach
Palo Alto Networks.

div.div:
The Bedrock credential fields shown here are the access key, secret,
and region pattern. Not yet confirmed in published documentation:
• Whether the integration can assume an IAM role (sts:AssumeRole
with an external ID) instead of holding a static access key. Many
security teams will not issue long-lived AWS keys at all.
• Whether Bedrock inference profiles and cross-region inference IDs
are selectable in model provisioning.
• Whether a single integration can span more than one AWS region,
or whether each region needs its own integration and slug.
• Whether PrivateLink to the Bedrock endpoint is supported from a
Hybrid data plane.
